steps.what: Capture production budgeting and scheduling inputs and resolve missing constraints
Compile budget totals and scheduled milestones for management review
Coordinate production plans, staffing, scheduling and marketing priorities with departments
Decide budgets and planning changes and communicate management instructions

tasks.design: Configure budget totals and milestone views in {PROJECT} using the producer's checked inputs from {SPREADSHEET}. The producer retains coordination, marketing choices and authority over plans and spending instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Management reviews required repeated collation of figures and dates from department records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing production planning software can hold schedules and budgets in a common view.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling creative goals, staff constraints and commercial priorities remains judgement and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: The producer makes trade-offs that departments can execute together.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive collation; management authority and coordination time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Plan technical resources against the production budget

evidence.claim: Yamdu provides production schedules and budgets; this supports testing native production management views.
The specific dashboard design and proposed savings are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is overall production management, excluding detailed scene pacing, equipment approval, staff progress meetings and marketing asset creation. Each shared activity must be assigned once across tasks.

Department leads already produce cost and availability records through unchanged planning work. Producer captures and verifies production version, cost item, amount, currency, committed or estimated status, milestone identifier, date, department and availability constraints in s1's 20 hours.

s2 only sums matching currency and status groups and displays recorded milestones; it does not choose schedules or infer availability. Missing data, conflicting dates and unsupported currency combinations remain visible and are resolved manually in s3 and s4. Additional department field upkeep is counted below.
Try native budget and milestone views first. s4 includes checking the view against source records before accepting instructions; no payment, booking or automatic marketing release is proposed.
unknowns: Whether records already have consistent cost categories and milestone identifiers
Whether repeated collation occupies the proposed baseline share
research_questions: Does a native view reduce collation while preserving budget status and availability caveats?

already_counted.description: Capture management fields, resolve exceptions and check proposed instructions

incremental.description: Maintain budget mappings and milestone view configuration

approvals.approved_version: Exact management instructions, budget snapshot, milestone version and negotiated constraints; edits void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15; less 6 focal upkeep gives central net=9. Range assumes some collation remains manual and most coordination and decisions are unchanged; 2 other-role hours are recorded outside the focal denominator.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify equipment and production elements through creative and practical assessment
Approve equipment, scenery, lights, props, costumes, choreography and music for the production

tasks.design: Keep the director's creative assessment and approval human, recording the accepted selection in {DOCS}. Native proposal records support traceability without replacing evaluation of the actual equipment and artistic elements.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficulty is suitability for a particular production rather than copying a list.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing proposal and document records already support the workflow; no new automation is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Creative fit, physical feasibility and interactions between elements require situated judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The director recognises how the selected elements affect the intended performance.
tasks.altitude: The director's week and approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess scenery against the intended performance

evidence.claim: Production element selection depends on creative and practical judgement; no task saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is assessment and approval of production elements, excluding purchasing, contract clearance, script breakdown and general budget management. Proposal preparation by department specialists remains their existing work outside this task.
Department specialists produce proposals and specifications; the director reads and checks them in s1. No structured suitability flag, automatic ranking or free new capture is assumed.
Keep current native document records. No implementation or incremental upkeep is proposed, so ongoing new work is zero. Recording the selection and approval remains within s2.
unknowns: Which elements require specialist safety or rights clearance before use
How authority is divided between producer and director
research_questions: Are accepted element versions and constraints traceable in the existing proposal record?

already_counted.description: Assess elements and approve the chosen combination

incremental.description: No changed process or new system upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact element selection, equipment specifications, creative versions and stated conditions; changes require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental focal upkeep=0. Physical assessment and creative approval remain fully human; no administrative saving is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review programs, time requirements and cast and set accessibility
Establish pace of programs and sequences of scenes with the cast and crew

tasks.design: Keep pacing decisions with the director, using the existing {PROJECT} availability record and script in {DOCS}. The director checks practical constraints and develops scene rhythm with the people performing it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clock time and availability do not determine artistic rhythm.
tasks.enabler_now: Current native schedule records can expose constraints without generating creative choices.
tasks.still_hard: Pace depends on performance, transitions and audience understanding.
tasks.human_edge: The director senses when a scene needs space or urgency and translates that into direction.
tasks.altitude: Pacing work and creative authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Continuity and the effect of duration on meaning

evidence.claim: Scene pacing combines artistic judgement with production constraints; a scheduling tool does not determine that judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is determining artistic program and scene pace, excluding resource scheduling, call sheet generation and editing execution. Those actions must not be counted again here.

Production coordinators produce cast availability and set access information in their existing scheduling work. Director reads, confirms and reconciles it in s1; uncertain or changed availability is clarified directly before direction in s2.
No machine action consumes structured availability and no free capture is assumed. Keep existing native records; no new implementation or ongoing upkeep means zero incremental work.
unknowns: Whether pacing is set during rehearsal, recording or edit review
Which timing constraints are firm and which can change
research_questions: Do current constraint records distinguish hard program duration from flexible scene rhythm?

already_counted.description: Review constraints and develop artistic pacing with performers

incremental.description: No changed process or new upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 with zero incremental upkeep. Both reading constraints and directing artistic pace keep their full time; no scheduling runtime is claimed as labour saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Conduct meetings with staff to discuss progress and resolve production objectives and obstacles

tasks.design: Keep the production progress meeting human. Existing {PROJECT} records can remain reference material while the producer hears concerns, tests progress claims and agrees corrective actions with staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on shared understanding and candid discussion rather than document production.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing meeting and project tools are sufficient; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Staff may disagree about progress, priorities and the causes of delays.
tasks.human_edge: The producer draws out concerns and secures realistic commitments.
tasks.altitude: Meeting time and responsibility for production objectives remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss production obstacles with technical departments

evidence.claim: Production progress discussion requires interpersonal coordination; no saving is inferred from availability of transcription tools.

assumptions: Boundary is the staff progress discussion itself, excluding preparing budget views, scene pacing and separate action execution; allocate shared coordination only once across tasks.

Staff produce progress accounts through their normal participation. Producer elicits and checks them during the full retained meeting time; no structured completion flag or free pre-meeting capture is assumed.
Use the current native project record if needed. No tool, recording or additional workflow is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether current meetings reveal obstacles early enough
Which corrective actions need separate specialist approval
research_questions: Do staff leave progress meetings with clear owners and feasible next actions?

already_counted.description: Hear staff accounts, resolve disagreements and agree next actions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Discussion and agreement remain fully human; no separate clerical baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A small reduction in repeated management collation leaves creative judgement, staff discussion and production decisions human.
reach: Discuss resource feasibility with media technical directors
Study scene rhythm with film and video editors
Assess scenery with set and exhibit designers
skills_to_grow: Verify budget and schedule source fields
Distinguish scheduling constraints from artistic pace
role.ambitious_version: Make well-grounded production decisions while keeping creative and interpersonal responsibility with the producer and director.
